title: Demo report download 404s: drop_start(analysis_id, 3) drops 'an-' but keeps the baked files keyed 'a-<name>' — every mock PDF is unreachable
evidence: demo_api.gleam:515-521+528: "/// maps to the application id ("a-aoife") which keys the baked PDF." / "let application_id = string.drop_start(analysis_id, 3)" / "let url = "/static/demo/report-" <> application_id <> ".pdf"" — demo_store.gleam:197 analysis ids are "an-aoife" (and an-conor/an-marta/an-declan/an-sara/an-tom/an-grace/an-liam at 208-274) — gleam_stdlib drop_start drops 3 leading graphemes: erl test "an-aoife" -> "aoife" — shipped assets are server/priv/static/demo/report-a-aoife.pdf, report-a-conor.pdf, report-a-declan.pdf, report-a-grace.pdf, report-a-liam.pdf, report-a-marta.pdf, report-a-sara.pdf, report-a-tom.pdf (all "a-" prefixed) — router.gleam:1298 missing static file -> "Error(_) -> wisp.not_found()"
detail: AC1 requires "download mock report" clickable in demo state; the download fetches /static/demo/report-aoife.pdf while the baked file is report-a-aoife.pdf, so all 8 downloads return 404 and surface an error. Contradicts the PR body claim "Download buttons serve the static bytes".
recommended_fix: Map analysis id to application id ("an-aoife" -> "a-aoife"), e.g. key demo_store.report_filenames by analysis id, or look up the application id from the store before building the URL. Verify each download in a browser.

title: pdf_prebake main() ignores its documented CLI argument
evidence: pdf_prebake.gleam:10-12: "////   gleam run -m demo/pdf_prebake -- server/priv" / "////   (cwd = server/; the arg is the priv dir. Defaults to "priv" relative" — pdf_prebake.gleam:472-473: "pub fn main() {" / "  let priv_dir = "priv"" (no argv read anywhere in the module)
detail: The usage comment promises the priv dir is passed as an argument, but main() hardcodes "priv" and never reads argv. From any cwd other than server/ the tool silently writes to <cwd>/priv and the documented argument cannot redirect it.
recommended_fix: Either parse the CLI argument (gleam/erlang os argv) and use it when provided, or drop the `-- server/priv` from the usage comment so the docs match the behavior.
